parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national entry screening is a universal exposure (binary sex on documents, refusal/tagging for suspected sex misrepresentation, reported confiscations and detentions of foreign trans travelers), and this state adds its own hostile layer: facility use mandated by birth sex with a shelter ban, an indecent-exposure definition covering bathroom use, a standing enforceable criminal ban on gender-expressive performance, birth-sex prison placement with care banned in custody, closed document changes, a panic defense, and documented police indifference. Killings of trans women at 7.8/100k exceed the national homicide baseline. Rule of law is operative but works against trans people here, which per the liability clause is exposure, not mitigation. For a travelling minor, the care ban and adult-assistance liability create direct exposure. No operative protective regime offsets this; highest-risk band boundary sits just below.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary sex-document rule; foreign-ministry cable instructs refusal and evidence demands on sex doubt; suspected misrepresentation can trigger permanent fraud ineligibility; documented confiscations/detentions of foreign trans travelers; foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; litigation against passport policy unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Any document/presentation mismatch at entry escalates into secondary inspection and possible fraud referral before state law is even reached.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State statute mandates birth-sex prison placement; gender-affirming care banned for inmates since April 2024; national corrections bureau policies described as cutting hormones; 2019 indecent-exposure definition can ground charges for bathroom use; drag statute carries up to 6 years on repeat.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented operating for trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A bathroom-trespass or indecency charge routes a visitor into a birth-sex custodial system.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: 2026 state act restricts all facilities to birth sex and bars trans women from women's shelters; 2019 indecent-exposure definition; nationwide patch of bans in government buildings, criminal in some states.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Warning-sign posting requirement struck down 2022; school-bathroom ban in litigation, unresolved.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access is unavoidable daily exposure; the documented trespass arrest of a trans student (state capitol, men's ward holding) shows the escalation path.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for under-18s banned including telehealth, upheld nationally June 2025; civil penalties for adults helping a minor obtain care; regret suits against parents/guardians; care banned for inmates.
care_services.interaction: A travelling parent with a trans minor risks state civil liability and prosecution-adjacent exposure; adult visitors cannot assume refills or continuity.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State criminalises 'male or female impersonators' performance; police and officials described turning a blind eye to assaults, treating venues as sin; national counterterrorism framing of 'radically pro-transgender' groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Chief-prosecutor 2019 opinion allows hate-crime enhancement for anti-trans violence, but state bias statute omits gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State enforcement and national hostile framing reinforce each other; performer-focused statute's application to everyday presentation unresolved.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban with provider and adult-assistant penalties; teacher outing-to-parents law (May 2024); sports bans; regret suits against guardians; foster/religious-refusal regime.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor converts ordinary school, medical or presentation friction into legal jeopardy for the guardian.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 10 recorded killings of trans women 2008–2025, 7.8/100k/yr, above national homicide baseline, treated as undercount floor; panic defence available; reported beatings and service refusal with police indifference.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; local municipal public-employment ordinances only, preempted for private sector.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims cannot rely on police or bias-statute recourse; recording agencies logged near-zero incidents, signalling under-recording.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Vehicle-licence marker suit unresolved; 2026 facility act not shown challenged; drag-ban application to visitors unresolved; school-bathroom litigation ongoing; civil-rights infrastructure thin and preempted.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment ruling (2020) and hate-crime statute remain; legal-aid FAQ exists for national document rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are partial, slow and mostly national-level; state-level recourse is effectively unavailable to visitors.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier of universal administrative exposure at entry and closed documents, but this jurisdiction adds documented above-baseline killings and criminal statutes (indecency definition, performance ban) that 0.35-A lacks; slightly worse on severity, similar on remedylessness.

0.55-C's worst feature is delayed/denied care with no custody threat; here facility exclusion is criminalised, shelters ban trans women, and killings exceed background, so this sits materially below that anchor.

0.15-C features organised morality sweeps with coerced detention and near-certain abuse on discovery; this dossier shows hostile law, elevated killings and indifference but no documented arrest pattern aimed at visitors for mere presentation, so it sits clearly above that anchor.

Comparable on birth-sex prison placement and criminalised presentation in state buildings, but this state adds above-background killing rates, a shelter ban, and national entry screening exposure; sits at or just below this anchor's band top.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is layered: national entry rules expose every trans visitor at the border (binary documents, refusal instructions, fraud findings, stranded travelers), and state law converts everyday life into exposure — facilities by birth sex with shelter exclusion, an indecent-exposure definition of bathroom use, an enforceable performance ban, birth-sex custody with care denied. Killings of trans women exceed the national homicide baseline and the panic defence plus police indifference leave thin recourse; the hate-crime enhancement opinion is untested as protection. For a travelling minor the care ban and adult-assistance penalties create direct legal jeopardy for the guardian. No documented protective machinery operates at state level; national litigation is unresolved. Severity on outing is elevated violence and jail (up to 60 days to 6 years under adjacent statutes), not execution; frequency of state targeting of visitors specifically is not documented. Net: firmly in the High Risk band, near its lower boundary, above organised-sweep jurisdictions.
